title: A twofold change in relative capture can remove count-weighted warming at 62 Finnish moth sites under a thermal bias bound
abstract: We derived a sharp bound on within-site community thermal trends under a stated thermal observation envelope. We applied it to 224,364 annual species records at 62 Finnish moth sites in 1993-2022, with external European thermal scores. A log capture-bias envelope of 0.01530 per year per C of species score permits a zero count-weighted trend. Across the 1.560 C interquartile score contrast, this is a 2.00-fold warm-relative-to-cold capture change over 29 years. The 95% spatial-block interval is 1.80 to 2.37; a block-and-year delta check gives 1.67 to 2.38. A common midpoint-anchor path reduces the spatially normalized response from 1.13 to 0.12 with a 1.85-fold capture change. The result does not show that capture changed. It sets a calibration target and gives a reproducible sensitivity method. The sharp bound excludes unknown static bias, unseen species and independent bias among equal-score species. It does not remove the previously published presence-weighted response or identify an ecological cause of weak thermal tracking.

display.caption: Corrected count-weighted thermal trends and the relative capture change that permits a zero trend. Intervals resample whole spatial blocks. The site-anchor zero has a sharp envelope interpretation; calendar paths are sensitivity scenarios.
